title: A highly sensitive liquid chromatography electrospray ionization mass spectrometry method for quantification of TMA, TMAO and creatinine in mouse urine
author: Veeravalli, Karu, et al.
materials: LLOQQC (Lowest Limit of Quantification Quality Control); (

Data acquisition and processing was performed using Thermo Xcalibur Version 2.2 software (Thermo Scientific, UK). Seven-point calibration curves were constructed for the concentration range 15–944 pg/μL for TMA and TMAO and 3.9–16000 pg/μL for creatinine, along with a blank urine sample. Peak area ratios of analyte to its internal standard (IS) were calculated as a function ratio of analyte concentration. Back calculations were performed from these curves to determine the concentration of analytes. Calibration curves and lower and upper limits of quantification (LLOQ or ULOQ) were according to the FDA guidance [29].

steps.title: Prepare TMA/TMAO aqueous standards
steps.instruction: Make working standards containing TMA and TMAO at 7.8, 15.6, 31.3, 62.5, 125, 250 and 500 ng/µL in water. For each concentration, mix 20 µL of the working standard with 5 µL water.

steps.title: Prepare urine samples for TMA/TMAO
steps.instruction: Thaw mouse urine to room temperature, then mix 5 µL urine with 20 µL water.

steps.title: Derivatize TMA/TMAO samples
steps.instruction: To 25 µL of each prepared aqueous standard or urine sample add 1 µL 2H9‑TMA (1 µg/µL), 2 µL 2H9‑TMAO (1 µg/µL), 1 µL concentrated ammonia and 30 µL ethyl bromoacetate (20 µg/µL in acetonitrile). Incubate 30 min at room temperature. Stop the reaction by adding 1 mL of 50 % acetonitrile, 0.025 % formic acid in water. Centrifuge at 15 700 × g for 3 min at room temperature. Transfer 100 µL supernatant and dilute to 1 mL with 50 % acetonitrile, 0.025 % formic acid in water. The resulting derivatized TMA and TMAO concentrations are 15, 30, 59, 118, 236, 472 and 944 pg/µL. Inject 20 µL onto a C18 column.

steps.title: Prepare creatinine stock and working solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare a creatinine stock solution (1 µg/µL) in water and an acetaminophen stock (20 µg/µL) in ethanol; store both at –20 °C. Prepare creatinine working standards at 0.24, 0.98, 3.91, 15.62, 62.5, 250 and 1000 ng/µL in 0.1 % formic acid in water.

steps.title: Prepare creatinine urine samples
steps.instruction: Thaw urine to room temperature. For each urine sample add 1 µL acetaminophen internal standard (20 µg/µL in ethanol) and then 998 µL 0.1 % formic acid. For each creatinine working standard, combine 16 µL standard, 1 µL acetaminophen (20 µg/µL) and 983 µL 0.1 % formic acid to obtain final creatinine concentrations of 3.9, 15.6, 62.5, 250, 1000, 4000 and 16000 pg/µL. Inject 20 µL onto a C18 column. Note: creatinine is measured after the TMA/TMAO analysis because derivatization affects it.

steps.title: Prepare TMA/TMAO calibration standards
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of each TMA‑TMAO working standard to 5 µL mouse urine (instead of water) and process exactly as described in the Derivatize TMA/TMAO samples step. The amount of TMA and TMAO in each calibration standard equals the sum of the spiked amount and the endogenous urine amount.

steps.title: Prepare creatinine calibration standards
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL mouse urine to 16 µL each creatinine working standard, then add 1 µL acetaminophen (20 µg/µL) and 982 µL 0.1 % formic acid. The final creatinine amount equals the sum of the spiked amount and the endogenous urine creatinine.

steps.title: Prepare QC standards
steps.instruction: Prepare quality‑control (QC) solutions for TMA/TMAO at 15 pg/µL (LLOQQC), 45 pg/µL (LQC), 400 pg/µL (MQC) and 750 pg/µL (HQC); and for creatinine at 4 pg/µL (LLOQQC), 12 pg/µL (LQC), 6400 pg/µL (MQC) and 12000 pg/µL (HQC).

steps.title: Acquire and process LC‑MS data
steps.instruction: Run all samples on LC‑MS using Thermo Xcalibur Version 2.2. Construct seven‑point calibration curves covering 15–944 pg/µL for TMA/TMAO and 3.9–16000 pg/µL for creatinine, including a blank urine sample. Calculate peak‑area ratios of analyte to internal standard, back‑calculate sample concentrations, and determine LLOQ/ULOQ according to FDA guidance.

steps.title: Method validation (refer to supplement)
steps.instruction: Validate the method for analyte separation, selectivity, sensitivity, LOD, LOQ, carry‑over, system suitability, accuracy, precision, dilution integrity, ruggedness, robustness, matrix effect and stability as described in the Supplementary data.
